foods/banana: "has tiny dark specks of seed running through its centre" - in seedless dessert bananas the specks are undeveloped vestigial seeds; a reader may not think of them as seeds
foods/butter: "is about four-fifths milk fat by weight" - 80% is the legal minimum in the US and EU; European-style butters run to about 82-86%
foods/egg: "sinks in a glass of water when fresh and floats when stale" - the standard kitchen test; ageing eggs usually tilt or stand on end before they actually float
foods/grape: "is toxic to dogs even in small amounts" - toxicity is well established but idiosyncratic; some dogs eat a few without harm
foods/honey: "is harvested from wax frames in late summer" - main harvest timing varies with region and climate, and frames belong to modern hives
"keeps almost indefinitely in a sealed jar without spoiling" - true of properly ripened low-moisture honey; high-moisture honey can ferment
foods/lemon: "grows on small, thorny evergreen trees in warm climates" - most lemon cultivars bear thorns, but some are nearly thornless
foods/mango: "has sap near the stem that can irritate the skin" - the sap contains urushiol-related compounds; it affects sensitive people, not everyone
foods/orange: "has a peel that can stay green on the tree in the tropics" - true (colour change needs cool nights), but may not be common knowledge to a reader
"is cut into wedges and handed out at half-time in youth sports" - a UK/US/Commonwealth custom, not universal
"is traditionally tucked into children's Christmas stockings" - a UK/US/Commonwealth custom, not universal
"has fragrant white blossom used in perfume and at weddings" - neroli is from the bitter-orange blossom; the bridal orange-blossom custom is largely historical
foods/strawberry: "has tiny seeds dotted over its outer surface" - botanically these are achenes (tiny fruits each holding a seed); everyday usage calls them seeds
foods/sushi: "began as a way to preserve fish in fermented rice" - refers to narezushi, the ancestral form; accurate but not everyday knowledge
